title: Transient Ops Clipboard: quick plays & temp procedures
body:
Purpose:
This is a personal quick-clipboard for late-night/short-handoff ops: compact triage steps, short-term mitigations, and notes to pass to the next pager. Not authoritative — copy the bits you need into the proper runbook/confluence if we use them more than twice.

Snapshot (what I saw at 02:15 PT):
- Alert: token-rate spike on hosted-api /v1/generate route (alert rule: token_rate_abnormal).
- Root cause suspicion: sudden increase in long-sequence requests from a single customer (cid: cust-214).
- Immediate impact: higher p99 latency (1.3s -> 4.6s) and CPU scheduling pressure on pool-gpu-a. No OOMs, KV cache miss rate increased.
- Actions taken: throttled offending key via rate-limit override, enabled model-fallback to lightweight-variant (redwood-llm-small-v2) for that key for 10m, reduced max-batch-size on pool-gpu-a, and warmed prefix-cache for popular prompts.

Quick triage checklist (5–10m):
1) Confirm alert details
   - prometheus query: increase in tokens_per_minute: rate(sum by(customer_id)(tokens_total{route="/v1/generate"})[5m])
   - note the origin IPs, customer_id, model and avg sequence length.
2) Check pool health
   - k get pods -n inference -l pool=pool-gpu-a
   - k logs -f <hot-pod> | rg -i "evict|slow|kvcache" --context 3
3) KV cache & prefix cache
   - check KV eviction metrics: kv_cache_evictions_total and kv_cache_miss_rate
   - if miss_rate > 10% and eviction rate spiked -> consider increase cache capacity on the pool (temporary) or force warm prefixes for top 50 prompts.
4) Decide immediate mitigation
   - Throttle offending API token if single key is the cause (use console -> API keys -> rate limit override). Keep note of TTL.
   - If multiple keys / noisy workload, enable routing to a cheaper / smaller model variant with fast response to drain pressure.
5) Temporary config changes (if needed)
   - Reduce batch size on pool: apply patch to k8s configmap "inference-batching" -> set max_batch_size: 16 (from 64). This reduces throughput but improves latency.
   - Disable continuous-batching for pool-gpu-a by setting batching.enabled=false (short window).
   - Re-enable after 10–30m when load normalizes.

Exact commands I used (copy/paste friendly):
- Check tokens by customer:
  curl -s -G 'https://prometheus.internal/api/v1/query' --data-urlencode 'query=rate(tokens_total{route="/v1/generate",customer_id="cust-214"}[5m])' | jq .
- View pods and tail logs:
  kubectl get pods -n inference -l pool=pool-gpu-a -o wide
  kubectl logs -n inference -f deploy/serving-runtime-pool-gpu-a -c runtime --tail=200 | rg -i "kvcache|evict|prefetch|error"
- Apply quick config (kustomize overlay patch):
  kubectl patch configmap inference-batching -n infra --type merge -p '{"data":{"max_batch_size":"16","continuous_batching":"false"}}'
  NOTE: use the k8s patch only if you are comfortable rolling back. Record the original values in the incident ticket.
- API key throttle (console): navigate to Console -> Keys -> select token -> Temporary throttle: 10 req/min for 20m -> save.

Model-fallback checklist (short window):
- Use fallback routing policy when pool latency > 2s and error rate < 0.5% to avoid false positives.
- Switch customer to redwood-llm-small-v2 for 10 minutes:
  - Console -> Routes -> customer overrides -> add override -> model=redwood-llm-small-v2 -> TTL=10m
- Observe quality complaints channel for the customer (if they respond, escalate to CS).

Temporary artifacts to leave for next oncall:
- Incident note: "Transient token flood from cust-214 at 02:05–02:18. Throttled key and routed to small model for 10m. Reduced batch size on pool-gpu-a. No OOMs. Follow-ups: check customer prompt patterns and consider per-customer prefix caching."
- JIRA ticket: OPS-842 (created to track follow-ups and permanent mitigations). Link added above.

Short restart safe-mode (if pod becomes unresponsive):
1) Attempt soft restart of the runtime container: kubectl rollout restart deploy/serving-runtime-pool-gpu-a -n inference
2) If pod stuck in CrashLoopBackOff, get diagnostics: kubectl describe pod <pod> -n inference; check dmesg on node for GPU driver errors.
3) If GPU driver OOMs/driver faults: cordon node, drain and move workloads while notifying infra on-call (pager: infra-oncall).

Emergency quickplays (2–5m):
- If control plane latency degrades across regions -> flip traffic to dedicated fallback region via smart-routing: Console -> Routing -> set policy priority: region=fallback-eu-1 first -> apply.
- If KV cache corrupted (symptoms: sudden high miss rate + bad responses): set kv_cache_readonly=true (config map) to avoid in-flight writes and schedule a maintenance restart during low traffic.

Unresolved / follow-ups (for next shift):
- Confirm whether cust-214 used a new long-prompt template; ask Solutions Eng for the prompt sample (PRIVILEGED).
- Make a small dashboard card for tokens-per-customer over 15m to help detect these spikes earlier.
- Evaluate automated per-key short-circuit fallback when sequence_length > 2048 (policy RFC).

Notes-to-self (on-call heuristics):
- Prefer routing to a smaller model instead of throttling customers if traffic is from known low-quality cohorts (we lose revenue otherwise).
- When reducing batch size, watch p50 and p95 spread — if p95 remains high but p50 drops, it's batching-induced latency.
- Always annotate the console change with TTL and brief rationale. It saves time for audits.

Post-shift checklist (what to hand off):
- Record the exact console/patch diffs in JIRA OPS-842.
- Leave the rate-limit override on the token with TTL until it expires; do NOT manually remove without confirming stability.
- Add a Slack thread summary in #ops-incidents with the short bullet list and link to the JIRA ticket.

If you're taking over:
- See "Snapshot" at top. Check that the TTLs for overrides have expired. If not and load normal: comment in JIRA and remove throttle only after confirming stabilization for 20m.
- If new alert triggers within 30m, escalate to oncall-2 and consider temporary maintenance window.

References (quick links):
- Confluence draft: /ops/serving-runtime-temp-fallbacks (linked above)
- Incident ticket: JIRA OPS-842
- PR that included fallback routing logic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1241

Last quick random thought:
- We should add a tiny per-key rate-limiter that steps in at queue depth > 1000 so the routing/fallback mechanism doesn't need to be touched in the middle of the night. If someone wants to pick it up, tag it as low-priority engineering backlog.

End of clipboard.

-- Maya R. (leaving this in users for fast handoff)
